***Topics:** Doppler effect and radial velocity • telescope power and resolution • dark matter evidence from rotation curves • solar system architecture and planetary properties • climates and habitability • exoplanet detection • tool transfer across Module 1*

**Estimated time:** ~4-5 hours

## Why this homework exists (read this)

_This is not busy work._ This assignment is a capstone for Lectures 10-12 and a bridge into exam prep. You are using the full Module 1 toolkit in realistic combinations: motion from Doppler shifts, temperature from thermal radiation, mass from orbits, and planet type from density.

This assignment is designed to:

- strengthen transfer across topics instead of treating each lecture as isolated,
- reinforce the Observable -> Model -> Inference workflow under mixed conditions,
- and prepare you for the Module 1 Exam on Friday, March 6.

## How to earn full credit

{{< include ../_includes/homework/how-to-earn-full-credit.qmd >}}

For this homework, show unit tracking and setup clearly on all calculation problems. For the mixed-tool prompts, state what is directly observed and what is inferred.

## Pro tips (to save time and pain)

- Do one pass for setup first: write knowns, unknowns, and tool/equation choice before calculating.
- For transfer problems, label each step with the tool you are using (for example: Doppler, Wien, Newton, transit depth).
- Use units as your lie detector.
- If a result feels extreme, do a quick order-of-magnitude sanity check before moving on.
- For exam prep, finish required problems first, then do the optional sprint in order.
